0.long_answer: The gene implicated in both Potocki–Lupski syndrome and Smith–Magenis syndrome is RAI1. In Potocki–Lupski syndrome, duplications of the RAI1 gene lead to the disorder, while in Smith–Magenis syndrome, deletions or loss-of-function mutations of the same gene are responsible. This reciprocal relationship highlights the key role of RAI1 gene dosage in these neurodevelopmental disorders, where an increase in gene copy number results in PTLS and a decrease causes SMS.
